slides.title: THE GRAMMAR REPAIR SHOP
slides.subtitle: Mastering 'Used To' vs 'Would' for Past Habits

items.text: IDENTIFY: The difference between past states and past actions.
REPAIR: Sentences by choosing the most precise grammatical structure.
PRODUCE: Accurate descriptions of your own childhood habits.

strategy_items.text: Think of 3 things you did as a child that you don't do now.
Share your memories with a partner using 'When I was 10, I...'

slides.title: BEN'S LIFE IN CHINA
slides.text: Let's look at Ben's experience living abroad. How did his habits change?

strategy_items.text: Complete the dialogue with the correct form of used to and short answers.

slides.title: BEN'S LIFE IN CHINA (PART 1)
slides.content:
Amy: Have you ever lived abroad?

Ben: Yes, I have. I lived in China for a few years.

Amy: (1) [REVEAL: Did you use to go] to school in China?

Ben: Yes, I (2) [REVEAL: did].

Amy: Wow, that's really cool. Why were you there?

slides.title: BEN'S LIFE IN CHINA (PART 2)
slides.content:
Ben: My mother (3) [REVEAL: used to work] for a company that had an office in Shanghai.

Amy: Shanghai? That's so interesting.

Ben: But you (4) [REVEAL: used to live] abroad, too, right? Was it Germany?

Amy: No, we didn't live there. But we (5) [REVEAL: used to visit] my grandparents there every summer.

slides.title: ACTIONS
slides.text:
Physical movements or repeated events.

I would walk to school every day.

slides.title: ACTIONS
slides.text:
Physical movements or repeated events.

I would walk to school every day.

slides.title: ACTIONS
slides.text:
Both options are correct for actions!

I would / used to play tennis.

slides.title: ACTIONS
slides.text:
Both options are correct for actions!

I would / used to play tennis.

slides.title: IS IT A STATE?
slides.text: Can you see it moving? No? It's a State!

points.text: ACTIONS: play, run, go, visit (Use 'Used to' or 'Would')
STATES: be, live, have, know, love (Use 'Used to' ONLY)

strategy_items.text: Decide if used to can be replaced with would. If it's a state verb, you can't!

slides.title: THE REPLACEMENT CHALLENGE (PART 1)
slides.content:
Taylor Wilson (1) used to dream about space. He (2) used to read books about science all the time. He (3) didn't use to spend much time playing games. He (4) used to go around talking to people about his ideas. Taylor (5) used to live in Arkansas before he moved to a bigger city.
1. [REVEAL: ---]
2. [REVEAL: would]
3. [REVEAL: wouldn't]
4. [REVEAL: would]
5. [REVEAL: ---]

slides.title: THE REPLACEMENT CHALLENGE (PART 2)
slides.content:
Brittany Wenger's parents (6) used to tell her she was too young to be a scientist. She (7) used to spend time looking at computer code every evening. She (8) didn't use to ignore her schoolwork, but she (9) used to get better grades in science than in history. Brittany (10) used to live in Ohio.
6. [REVEAL: would]
7. [REVEAL: would]
8. [REVEAL: wouldn't]
9. [REVEAL: would]
10. [REVEAL: ---]

strategy_items.text: Complete the sentences. Watch out for 'be' and 'live'!

slides.title: SENTENCE REPAIR
slides.content:
1. In the summer, the kids [REVEAL: would / used to] often stay up late.
  2. The students [REVEAL: used to] be strangers.
  3. I [REVEAL: used to] cycle to school.
  4. My dad [REVEAL: used to] work as a lawyer.
  5. We [REVEAL: used to] live in a house.

slides.title: MY LIFE, THEN AND NOW
slides.text: Think of a major change in your life. Write 3 sentences about your habits and states before the change using used to and would.

slides.title: TASK 4: STUDENT COLLABORATION
slides.content: Share your sentences with your group. Check for correct use of used to (states/habits) and would (actions only).
